[=Compilation Pipeline=]

[==Two Input Paths, One Backend Boundary==]

[.mermaid
|flowchart LR
|	SPO[".SPO Text"] --> TOK["mTokenizer"]
|	TOK --> SPO_P["mSPO_Parser"]
|	SPO_P --> SPO_AST["mSPO_AST"]
|	SPO_AST --> DES["mSPO_Desugar"]
|	DES --> TYP["mSPO_AST_Types"]
|	TYP --> LOW["mSPO2IL"]
|	LOW --> IL["mIL_AST"]
|
|	ILT[".ILT Text"] --> TOK2["mTokenizer"]
|	TOK2 --> IL_P["mIL_Parser"]
|	IL_P --> IL
|
|	IL --> OPC["mIL_GenerateOpcodes"]
|	OPC --> PROC["mVM_Data.tProcDef[]"]
|	PROC --> VM["mVM"]
.]

[.txt|.SPO.] and [.txt|.ILT.] use the same lexer and meet afterward in
[.txt|mIL_AST.tModule.].

[==1. Tokenization==]

[.txt|mTokenizer.] is the shared lexer for both frontends.

Key facts from the code:

- reserved special characters live in [.txt|ReservedChars.]
- [.txt|#.] and [.txt|§.] create [.txt|SpecialId.] tokens
- string literals can be single-line or multi-line
- char literals are currently limited to alphanumeric single characters
- identifiers may contain [.txt|....], which is how operator-style names are formed

Both the SPO parser and the IL parser operate on [.txt|mTokenizer.tToken.].

[==2. SPO Parsing==]

[.txt|mSPO_Parser.] builds the richer surface AST in [.txt|mSPO_AST.].

The SPO frontend knows, among other things:

- modules with [.txt|§IMPORT.], commands, and [.txt|§EXPORT.]
- patterns, typed patterns, and guard patterns
- lambdas and methods
- [.txt|§IF.], [.txt|§IF ... MATCH.], [.txt|§IS.]
- tuples, pairs, prefix/tag values, and records
- mutable values via [.txt|§VAR.] and [.txt|§TO_VAL.]
- type literals as normal expressions
- pipe syntax in both directions

The parser defaults a missing [.txt|§IMPORT.] section to an empty record pattern.
[.txt|§EXPORT.] remains mandatory.

[==3. Desugaring==]

[.txt|mSPO_Desugar.] reduces the surface language to a smaller core.

Important rewrites:

- tuple expressions and tuple patterns become nested pairs
- text literals become char lists via [.txt|#_Char... <int>.]
- [.txt|expr §IS pattern.] becomes [.txt|§IF expr MATCH { pattern: §TRUE; _: §FALSE }.]
- pipe expressions are reordered into normal call chains
- tuple types are desugared into pair types

Not everything is normalized equally:

- [.txt|DesugarType.] actively handles only tuple types today
- many other type nodes are currently passed through unchanged

[==4. Type Analysis and Scope Construction==]

[.txt|mSPO_AST_Types.] annotates expressions and patterns directly in the AST with [.txt|mVM_Type.tType.].

[.mermaid
|sequenceDiagram
|	participant Parser as mSPO_Parser
|	participant Desugar as mSPO_Desugar
|	participant Types as mSPO_AST_Types
|	participant Lower as mSPO2IL
|
|	Parser->>Desugar: tModuleNode
|	Desugar->>Types: desugared commands + import pattern
|	Types->>Types: UpdatePatternTypes(import)
|	loop for each command
|		Types->>Types: UpdateCommandTypes(command, scope)
|	end
|	Types->>Lower: annotated AST
.]

Type analysis does three things at the same time:

- it computes types for expressions
- it binds new names into scope through patterns
- it checks contracts such as [.txt|if.] conditions or method arguments
- it does not start with an empty scope in the interpreter, but with a built-in [.txt|_=....] proc for [.txt|§VAR.] assignments inside method-call chains

Important semantics:

- block types are the union of all possible [.txt|§RETURN.] results
- [.txt|Call.] uses [.txt|mVM_Type.Infer(...).]
- [.txt|IfMatch.] propagates the matched value type into each case
- [.txt|VarToVal.] explicitly requires a [.txt|[[§VAR T]].] type

[==5. Module Wrapper and Lowering to IL==]

[.txt|mSPO2IL.MapModule(...).] does not translate a SPO module directly into a def list. It first builds a synthetic initialization lambda:

[.txt
|ImportPattern => {
|	Commands
|	RETURN ExportExpression
|}
.]

That lambda is type-checked once more and then lowered into IL.

The lowering step produces:

- a type-definition block for [.txt|mIL_AST.]
- a list of [.txt|§DEF.] blocks
- explicit register IDs ([.txt|r_*.]) and def IDs ([.txt|d_*.])
- helper procedures for lambdas, methods, recursion, and pattern matching

Important for matches:

- [.txt|mSPO2IL.] compiles cases into helper functions
- successful matches are internally encoded via a [.txt|#Result ....] prefix
- failure is transported as [.txt|().]

[==6. IL AST and Text Form==]

[.txt|mIL_AST.] is the shared boundary for:

- IL generated from [.txt|.SPO.]
- directly parsed [.txt|.ILT.]

[.txt|mSPO_Parser.Module.ParseText(...).ToILT().] is the practical helper path for:

- regression artifacts under [.txt|SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/*.ILT.]
- the [.txt|.SPO.] vs [.txt|.ILT.] comparison inside [.txt|mModule.Init(...).]
- canonical renumbering to textual [.txt|t_*.] and [.txt|d_*.] IDs before writing IL text

The text form always starts with [.txt|§TYPES.] and is followed by one or more [.txt|§DEF.] sections.

[==6a. SPO Notation and IL Notation Are Not Identical==]

When reading [.txt|.SPO.] and [.txt|.ILT.], it is important to note that not only the format changes, but also some keywords:

[| [*Meaning*] | [*SPO*] | [*IL*] |]
[| recursive type | [.txt||§RECURSIVE.] | [.txt||§REC.] |]
[| generic type | [.txt||§GENERIC.] | [.txt||§ALL.] |]
[| interface type | [.txt||§INTERFACE.] | [.txt||§ANY.] |]

This is not a cosmetic side detail, but a real architectural boundary:

- [.txt|mSPO_Parser.] builds the richer surface AST
- [.txt|mSPO2IL.] then serializes into the more compact IL notation
- [.txt|mIL_Parser.] only reads that IL notation back in

Additional observations from the code:

- the parsed-module [.txt|ToILT().] helper currently lives in [.txt|mSPO_Interpreter.], not in [.txt|mSPO_Parser.]
- that helper is practical today, but it still couples parsing, desugaring, type analysis, and lowering more tightly than necessary
- debug output introduces a third internal notation through [.txt|mVM_Type.ToText(...).], for example interface types as [.txt|§LET ... IN ....] and generics as [.txt|[[t => T]].]

[==7. IL to Opcodes==]

[.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.GenerateOpcodes(...).] translates IL into:

- [.txt|mVM_Data.tProcDef<tPos>.] for each definition
- concrete register indices
- concrete [.txt|mVM_Data.tOpCode.] instructions

At the same time, it checks type-safety constraints through [.txt|mVM_Type.], such as:

- call arguments
- result types of [.txt|§RETURN.]
- the shape of [.txt|TRY_AS_*.] commands
- var set/get contracts

[==8. Hand-off to the VM==]

At this point the frontend and IL layers are finished. The remaining work is runtime execution over [.txt|mVM_Data.tData.], no longer AST or source text.

[.txt|mVM.Run(...).] has two relevant modes:

- execution of an IL module
- execution of an already materialized proc or extern proc

For module execution there is an additional fixed startup contract:

- [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] returns a def list in module order
- the last def is executed as the init proc
- all earlier defs are packed into [.txt|ENV.] as a [.txt|Def.] tuple
- the resolved import record is passed in as [.txt|ARG.]
- [.txt|OBJ.] starts as [.txt|().]

The runtime-side details are documented in [<../30_runtime/31_vm_and_modules.wiki|31_vm_and_modules.wiki>].

That completes the pipeline:

o 1. Read text
o 2. Tokenize
o 3. Optionally parse SPO into AST
o 4. Desugar
o 5. Type-check
o 6. Lower to IL
o 7. Turn IL into opcodes and [.txt|tProcDef.]
o 8. Execute in the register-based VM
